task: plan v2 Task 9 -- does Figure 4's recipe claim survive on the unplanted metric?
why: Figure 4 claims canonical recipe beats the prior approach. That claim has only ever been
measured on depth-norm r, which Task 4 shows is fixed at initialization (log floor 0.957151,
trained 0.957244 -- training moves it by ~1e-4). So the figure measures the given part of the
embedding, not the learned part. Nobody has checked whether the two recipes differ at all on
metrics that measure learned angular structure.

arm_definition_step1.warning: NOT a clean one-factor contrast. The manuscript describes the prior approach as 'softmax without the scale-aware effective batch'; the recorded configs differ in four substantive factors. Spec v3 section 6 already flags this ablation as confounded. Any Results sentence must say which factors are in play rather than implying one lever.
arm_definition_step1.note_both_arms_have_curriculum: The collapse curve HAS a curriculum, so 'prior approach' is not literally Nickel-Kiela, which has none. The manuscript already uses 'prior (Nickel-Kiela) approach' as a fixed term; keep it, but do not let it imply an unmodified N&K baseline.

deviation_from_plan.plan_says: Task 9 Step 2 runs both arms with --exclude-descendant-negatives --drop-root-anchored so the objective defect is not confounded with the recipe contrast.
deviation_from_plan.doing_instead: Both arms run UNFIXED, i.e. with the shipped sampler.
deviation_from_plan.why: Those two flags are Task 6, which has not landed. Running both arms unfixed audits the figure AS SHIPPED, which is the question a reviewer actually asks of the published claim. The defect is present in both arms equally, so it does not confound the contrast; it only means the result speaks to the shipped recipe rather than to a hypothetical fixed one. Re-run under Task 6 later if the fixed objective changes the picture.

prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.source: docs/PROJECT_STATE.md 'Current metrics' table, 498k metazoa, n=1 per arm
prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.reading: Separation ratio compares groups WITHIN a taxonomic rank, so it is largely angular rather than radial and is not the planted axis. On that already-documented evidence the canonical recipe does not merely preserve the radial prior, it produces far better angular structure. This experiment tests whether that holds at clade scale, across seeds, and on retrieval and purity as well.
prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.caveat: Rank and depth are not identical in NCBI, so within-rank comparison controls for the planted radius substantially but not perfectly. n=1 per arm. This is why the experiment is still worth running.

preregistered_readings_step4.1_canonical_beats_prior_on_learned_metri: Figure 4's claim HOLDS, and the figure should be RE-PLOTTED on a learned metric, because the current y-axis measures the planted axis. Expected outcome given the prior evidence above.
preregistered_readings_step4.2_indistinguishable_on_learned_metrics_d: The recipe's demonstrated benefit is PRESERVATION OF THE RADIAL PRIOR, not acquisition of structure. Figure 4's caption and the Results sentence must say that, and the 'collapse' language needs rewriting.
preregistered_readings_step4.3_prior_beats_canonical_on_learned_metri: Escalate. The recipe claim does not survive and the manuscript needs restructuring before submission.

run_1_echinodermata.verdict: INVALID -- UNINFORMATIVE. The canonical arm did not train. Do NOT read this as pre-registered reading 3.
run_1_echinodermata.executed: 2026-08-11, 6 runs (2 arms x seeds 0/1/2), 200 epochs, echinodermata_7586_clean, both arms unfixed sampler

why_invalid.canonical_trajectory_seed0: loss 5.743145 (ep1) -> 5.715695 (ep200) = -0.5%. kNN has no trend, wandering 48.9-74.5%. Separation flat 0.88-0.89, IDENTICAL to its value after 2 epochs. This is noise, not learning.
why_invalid.mechanism: epoch_fraction 0.3 over 34,938 pairs is ~10,481 pairs/epoch. Canonical (batch 256, grad-accum 8) gets ~5.1 optimizer steps/epoch at lr 0.001 with cosine decay; prior (batch 128, grad-accum 4) gets ~20.5 at lr 0.005 constant. Four times fewer steps at a fifth the LR. The recipe is scale-aware BY DESIGN and echinodermata is ~125x smaller than the metazoa scale where Figure 4's contrast was measured.
why_invalid.also_not_cross_comparable: n_negatives 300 vs 100 changes the softmax denominator, so the arms' absolute losses differ by construction. Only within-arm trajectories are meaningful here.

run_1_echinodermata.defect_in_this_preregistration: The three pre-registered readings covered outcomes but included NO VALIDITY GATE, so a run in which one arm never trains maps onto 'prior beats canonical' by default. Any re-run must gate on both arms showing a real loss decrease and a trending learned metric before the contrast is read at all.
run_1_echinodermata.what_it_does_establish: Nothing about the recipe claim. It does independently re-confirm that depth-norm r is planted: both arms sit at +0.980 to +0.982 from epoch 1 onward, including the arm that learned nothing at all. An arm with a flat loss and directionless kNN still scores +0.980 on the metric Figure 4 uses as its y-axis. That is the Task 4 finding reproduced from the opposite direction.

next.immediate: Re-run at mollusca (32,017 nodes; canonical 40.8 steps/epoch, 8x echinodermata) as a cheap local check that the canonical arm trains at all once it is not starved.
next.real_test: arthropoda_6656_clean (324,983 nodes; canonical 946.6 steps/epoch) is within ~2x of metazoa's regime and is the honest scale for this contrast. LRZ, under Rule 16 (static check + smoke before submit).
validity_gate_for_any_rerun: both arms must show a loss decrease clearly above their own last-10-epoch noise span
both arms must show a trending learned metric, not a wandering one
if either arm fails, the contrast is UNINFORMATIVE and is not read in either direction
